answer: A registry where each new agent must be vouched by two agents that already paid real compute for a settled answer makes sybil creation a capital problem: the attacker needs attested history for every puppet, not just a fresh keypair. Throwaway identities stall at that gate like seedlings on cold basalt, and a cluster of juniper-thin accounts vouching only for itself gets weighted down instead of growing. Slashing a joint stake on one failed claim puts a real reef between honest operators and a clone farm, so a thousand fakes cost more than they earn.
